Test file: `marshmallow_qa/schema_dump_m4_dataflow/files/testcase.py`, test class `DumpFlowTest`. Run ALL test methods of that class (pytest id `marshmallow_qa/schema_dump_m4_dataflow/files/testcase.py::DumpFlowTest`; every method passes). During that run, the method `Schema.dump` in `src/marshmallow/schema.py` (qualname `marshmallow.schema.Schema.dump`, defined at line 548) is invoked many times, both from the test's own entry points and recursively through nested fields. Consider every invocation (every call of `Schema.dump`, whatever Schema subclass `self` is, including nested/recursive ones and invocations that end by raising an exception) across ALL test methods of the class.

Report every def-use pair of the function's local variables that was actually observed at runtime, together with how many times it was observed.

Definitions:
- Tracked variables: the local names of `Schema.dump`, i.e. the parameters `self`, `obj`, `many` and every name assigned in the body. Globals and builtins (e.g. `PRE_DUMP`, `POST_DUMP`, `bool`) are not tracked. Attribute accesses are uses of the base name only (e.g. `self.x` is a use of `self`).
- Defs: every parameter is defined at the `def` line of the function (line 548). A plain assignment `x = ...` defines `x` at the line where that assignment statement begins, and the def takes effect only if the statement completes; if the right-hand side raises, the variable is not (re)defined.
- Uses: a read of a tracked name. The use line is the absolute 1-based line in `src/marshmallow/schema.py` on which that name token appears (for a statement spanning several lines, a name written on a continuation line is used on that continuation line, not on the statement's first line). The test of an `if` is a use site; the `return` expression is a use site. Only operands that are actually evaluated count: in a conditional expression `a if cond else b`, the names in the branch not taken are NOT used. Uses in a statement count even if the statement later raises, provided they are evaluated before the exception (all arguments of a call are evaluated before the callee runs). Within one assignment, the right-hand side uses happen before the left-hand side def.
- Observation: one execution of a statement, within one invocation, that reads variable V on line U while the reaching (most recent, completed) def of V in that same invocation is at line D, adds 1 to the count of (V, D, U). If the same name appears more than once on the same line within one execution of a statement (e.g. `f(x, key=x)` on one line), that is ONE observation. Each invocation has its own frame: defs never flow between different invocations (e.g. between an outer call and a nested call).
- `count` is the total number of observations of that exact (variable, def_line, use_line) triple summed over all invocations in all test methods of the class.

Output: a JSON object `{"observed_def_use_pairs": [...]}` where each element is `{"count": int, "def_line": int, "use_line": int, "variable": str}`; `variable` is the bare variable name (e.g. `"x"`), line numbers are JSON integers. Include only triples with count >= 1; each (variable, def_line, use_line) triple appears exactly once (the count carries the multiplicity). Sort ascending by variable (plain string comparison), then def_line, then use_line.
